The leaf shows scattered dark black/sooty spots and patches distributed across the surface, with the underlying leaf tissue remaining greenish. The spots are superficial-looking, non-necrotic, and have a dusty/sooty appearance — consistent with fungal growth on the leaf surface rather than tissue death or lesions penetrating the leaf.

Key observations:
- Dark, black powdery/sooty deposits scattered across the leaf
- No water-soaked or necrotic lesions (rules out Anthracnose)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- No tip/branch dieback symptoms (rules out Die_Back)
- Superficial black fungal growth on green tissue — classic Sooty Mould pattern
